t: Knossos grew from the ruins of the Minoan palace into one of the two leading Greek city-states of Iron Age Crete.
It was governed by annual kosmoi and a council of elders, with men's messes and age groups for citizen training.
Long rivalry with Gortyn and Lyttos ended when Quintus Caecilius Metellus conquered Crete for Rome in 69–67 BCE.
dyk: Classical Knossos put the Labyrinth on its silver coins, sometimes with the Minotaur, centuries after the Bronze Age palace that inspired the legend had fallen into ruin.
ev: Rich burials in the North Cemetery show Knossos among the wealthiest Aegean towns
Treaty between Knossos and Tylissos made under the arbitration of Argos
Knossos begins striking silver coins showing the Labyrinth
Knossos seizes and destroys its rival Lyttos in the Lyttian War
Philip V of Macedon becomes protector of the Cretan Koinon
Cretans defeat the Roman fleet of Marcus Antonius near Kydonia
Quintus Caecilius Metellus conquers Crete, including Knossos
